judge_reasoning: The model's plan illegally attacks with Angel of Invention and two newly-created Servo tokens, all of which have summoning sickness (no haste) and cannot attack the turn they enter the battlefield. Once these illegal attackers are removed, only 3 creatures (Cutthroat, Aristocrat, Sacred Cat) can attack. The opponent has exactly 3 blockers, and while skulk guarantees Cutthroat is unblocked, the opponent can block both remaining attackers, limiting damage to just 2 (Cutthroat only), leaving the opponent at 1 life instead of the required ≤0. Since the rest of the plan (sacrificing creatures to Ayli, then exiling Gideon) only removes protection but deals no additional damage, exiling Gideon would not cause the opponent to lose if their life is still positive. The solution therefore fails to guarantee victory against a reasonable/optimal blocking decision by the opponent, unlike the official solution's trick of pumping power after blocks are locked in.
model_solution:
1. Cast Angel of Invention (tap 2 Plains + 3 Swamps), choosing Fabricate 2 to create two 1/1 Servo tokens. Other creatures get +1/+1: Vampire Cutthroat 2/2, Indulgent Aristocrat 2/2, Sacred Cat 2/2, both Servos 2/2, Ayli 3/4.
2. Attack with Vampire Cutthroat, Indulgent Aristocrat, Sacred Cat, Angel of Invention, and both Servos (6 attackers). Ayli stays home (its damage is prevented anyway).
   - Cutthroat (skulk, power 2) can't be blocked by any of the opponent's creatures (all have power >2): 2 damage guaranteed.
   - Opponent has only 3 potential blockers for the other 5 attackers, so at least 2 more 2-power attackers connect. Total combat damage to the opponent is at least 6, putting them at -3 or lower (they don't lose yet due to the emblem).
   - Lifelink: Cutthroat, Aristocrat, Sacred Cat, and Angel each deal their 2 damage to either the opponent or a blocker, so I gain exactly 8 life regardless of blocks: 21 → 29.
3. Postcombat main phase (5 lands untapped): Activate Ayli's first ability ({1}, tap a Swamp), sacrificing a surviving creature (at least 3 of the 6 attackers survive since at most 3 can be blocked). Gain at least 1 life (toughness ≥1) → at least 30 life. (If for some reason still short, one more spare land allows a second {1} sacrifice.)
4. With ≥30 life (at least 10 more than starting life), activate Ayli's second ability ({1}{W}{B}: Plains, Plains, Swamp), sacrificing another creature, targeting Gideon of the Trials. Gideon is exiled.
5. The opponent no longer controls a Gideon planeswalker, so the emblem no longer protects them. State-based actions see their life total at 0 or less, and they lose the game.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

</solution>

content.thinking:
Since Gideon's emblem prevents loss while they control a Gideon planeswalker, I need to kill Gideon first before finishing them off with 3 damage. I'm working through our board state: 10 lands, 21 life, and considering Ayli's exile ability which requires being at 30 life to activate.

Ayli itself can't deal damage due to Gideon's +1 effect, so I need another damage source while using lifegain from sacrificing creatures to hit that 30-life threshold. I'm eyeing Declaration in Stone to clear out both Renegade Ralliers as blockers, leaving only Bruna, and looking at Angel of Invention's fabricate mode to boost lifelink creatures for the life gain plan.

Even if the opponent doesn't block, they can't lose to lethal damage while Gideon's emblem is active—but once we exile Gideon with Ayli, state-based actions should immediately check their life total and finish them off if it's already at zero or below.

So the plan is combat damage first to drop their life, then post-combat use remaining mana to gain life back to 30 via sacrifices before exiling Gideon, since Gideon can't do anything at instant speed with no mana. Now I need to map out mana allocation across all the different blocking scenarios, starting with the 3 mana needed for Ayli's exile ability.

I'm working through casting Angel of Invention to add two Servo tokens, then calculating remaining mana for sacrifices—each sacrifice through Ayli's first ability costs 1 and gains life equal to the sacrificed creature's toughness, so I need to figure out which creatures to sacrifice to reach exactly 9 extra life.

Actually, combat with lifelink looks more promising—attacking with Cutthroat, Aristocrat, Sacred Cat, and Angel all carrying lifelink could rack up life gain, and I'm checking whether Cutthroat's skulk ability lets it slip past the opponent's bigger blockers unblocked.

Working through the lifelink math, blocked or not, each attacker's power still converts to life gained, so those four creatures could net around 8 life total—just short of the 9 I need, pushing me to look for one more point somewhere else.

I'm now checking mana: after Angel of Invention costs, I have 5 left, enough to sacrifice a Servo for toughness and exile Gideon by sacrificing another creature, using all 9 mana with just one to spare. Then I still need to verify lethal damage gets through—opponent's at 3 life, has three blockers available, but Cutthroat's skulk ability makes it unblockable for 2, so I'm counting which other attackers can slip past to close out the last point of damage.

Since damage and lifelink resolve simultaneously, if Angel dies mid-combat the Servos drop to 1/1, but sacrificing still nets 1 life, bringing the total to exactly 30 — meeting the threshold. If Angel survives instead, the Servos stay at 2 toughness and the total lands even higher at 31, so the condition holds either way.

With extra mana left after casting Angel and paying for exile (8 of 10 used), I can sacrifice twice for two life bumps, reaching 31. Exile also demands sacrificing a separate creature, so I'm tallying likely combat losses — Bruna and Rallier could each kill one blocker — leaving plenty of survivors among the six attackers plus Ayli to cover both sacrifice costs comfortably.

The lifelink boost still triggers as long as blocked creatures connect with their blockers, which they will regardless of how many creatures gang up to block, so that 8 life gain looks solid. I'm now wondering if the puzzle actually hinges on Declaration in Stone or Stasis Snare instead, so I want to double check that angle.

Actually, sacrificing 1/1s repeatedly via Ayli isn't efficient enough to reach 9 life pre-combat, and Ayli doesn't need to deal damage herself so prevention isn't an issue. Once Gideon is exiled the "opponents can't win" emblem stops mattering, and state-based actions will make the opponent lose the moment their life hits zero or below — that total persists even at negative values, so the win locks in as soon as Ayli's ability resolves. I want to verify whether there's another way to close out damage after exiling Gideon, just as a safety net.

Working through the combat math: skulk on Cutthroat guarantees it's unblockable since every opposing creature (Bruna at 5, Ralliers at 3) has power greater than 2, so it connects along with at least two more unblocked attackers for six-plus damage against the opponent's three life, putting them well below zero. Even if they don't block at all, twelve damage comes through and I gain eight life. Either way I land at 29 life post-combat with five mana still open — enough to sacrifice a creature for the extra life boost and then pay to exile Gideon while sacrificing another creature, keeping the mana and color requirements covered comfortably across my Plains and Swamps.

To be extra safe I could sacrifice twice to push past 30 life using my last land, since I'll have plenty of survivors from the attack plus Ayli to spare for sacrifices. I'm leaning toward fabricating into servos rather than counters since more bodies gives me more sacrifice fodder. Ayli should stay back rather than attack, since there's no benefit to sending her in.

4534:702.72b The two abilities represented by champion are linked. See rule 607, “Linked Abilities.”
5464:704.5a If a player has 0 or less life, that player loses the game.
